title: Agentic AI and the Vulnerability of the White-Collar Circular Flow
summary: The transition from simple chatbots to autonomous agentic AI workflows marks a shift in automating complex intellectual labor, driving short-term corporate profit margins and stock valuations. However, as companies aggressively substitute human white-collar labor with digital agents to lower costs, they risk destabilizing the macroeconomic circular flow. Without adequate wage income, displaced knowledge workers cannot consume, which will eventually depress the corporate revenues of the very firms leading the automation wave. For finance professionals, assessing long-term corporate viability now requires evaluating how resilient a company's customer base is against systemic labor market displacement.

title: Sovereign Wealth Funds as Arbiters of AI-Driven Wealth Redistribution
summary: As AI-driven productivity gains concentrate unprecedented financial capital within a few dominant tech monopolies, traditional labor markets are failing to distribute economic gains equitably. To prevent a collapse in aggregate consumer demand, public institutions and sovereign wealth funds are increasingly investing in AI infrastructure to secure broad-based asset ownership for the general public. Recirculating these massive AI corporate profits back to citizens through public dividends and pensions represents a vital macroeconomic counterweight to labor income decline. This shift ensures that the wealth created by intellectual automation continues to circulate and support systemic economic stability.

title: Revaluing Human Capital: The Urgency of Education Reform in the AI Era
summary: Because generative AI automates routine cognitive tasks like coding and financial modeling, the premium on traditional rote-learning education is rapidly evaporating. To preserve the income-consumption link, educational systems must urgently transition toward teaching non-automatable skills such as problem-defining, ethical judgment, and complex negotiation. For business students, human capital must no longer be viewed as a cost to minimize, but as a strategic asset capable of steering AI productivity toward novel market opportunities. Cultivating these creative competencies is essential to maintaining high-wage employment and sustaining the consumer demand that drives global markets.

title: AI Capex Surges Amid Sovereign Wealth Shifting: The Impending Circular Flow Dilemma
summary: As major technology firms dramatically scale capital expenditure on AI infrastructure, financial markets price in unprecedented short-term productivity gains and margin expansions. However, for a finance specialist like Jaehyuk Song, the long-term systemic risk lies in the disruption of the macroeconomic circular flow: if AI-driven intellectual automation permanently displaces high-wage service sectors, aggregate consumer purchasing power will collapse, eventually erasing the corporate revenues that justify today's valuations. To sustain long-term market demand, institutional investors must shift focus from immediate cost-cutting metrics to broader wealth distribution mechanisms, such as sovereign wealth funds and democratized asset ownership.

title: Beyond Short-Term EBITDA: Why Broad-Based ETF Ownership is Critical for AI-Era Consumption
summary: Modern corporate strategies increasingly prioritize AI integration to optimize intellectual labor costs, boosting immediate cash flows and equity valuations. Yet, this microeconomic efficiency threatens macroeconomic stability by eroding labor income, leading to reduced consumer spending on housing, autos, and discretionary goods. For future finance professionals, the viability of these business models depends on solving this distribution crisis through structural reforms like broader retail ETF and pension ownership. Sustained financial prosperity in the AI age will ultimately rely on how effectively capital markets can circulate productivity gains back into the hands of consumers.
